page: Microsoft Azure E8-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configuration designed for workloads requiring a substantial memory footprint with low compute overhead. Powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a constrained CPU layout providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads, accompanied by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 32.0 GB per vCPU.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a 137 GB solid-state drive (SSD), offering localized low-latency scratch space. The platform does not bundle hardware GPU accelerators and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware instruction set extensions include standard AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptography suites, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX instructions.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2693.59 and Geekbench single-core reaching 1587.0. However, multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit, as reflected in a multi-core Geekbench score of 1978.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 2693.59. Memory subsystem throughput benchmarks record 33.33 GB/sec on uncached 256MB read operations and 22.24 GB/sec on writes, alongside a PassMark memory score of 2110.57. Redis operations registered 2.06 million SET operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 2.57 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained core architecture allows deployments that require substantial memory capacity to lower software licensing fees tied to per-core pricing models. This profile fits memory-resident databases, caching tiers, ETL staging jobs, and operational data stores that do not demand extensive parallel compute resources.
description: Microsoft Azure E8-2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it couples 64.0 GB of RAM with a 137 GB local SSD, delivering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per core. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic hardware support, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight solid single-thread performance alongside bounded multi-threaded processing due to the dual-thread ceiling. Memory benchmarks demonstrate stable mid-tier throughput, making this server profile technically suited for memory-intensive caching layers, in-memory key-value databases, and lightweight ETL pipelines where RAM capacity outweighs multi-core compute demands.
